title: Affine calculation of fibres of a finite pushforward
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $B$ be a finite $A$-algebra, let $V=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ and $X=\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $s\in V$ have residue field $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. For the induced finite morphism $f:X\to V$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], the canonical map $(f_*\mathcal O_X)_s\otimes_{\mathcal O_{V,s}}\kappa(s)\to\Gamma(X\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s),\mathcal O)$ is an isomorphism, identified under the affine descriptions with $B\otimes_A\kappa(s)\cong B\otimes_A A_s/\mathfrak m_sA_s$ [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra].

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ be the prime of $s$, so $A_s=A_{\mathfrak p}=\mathcal O_{V,s}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-free-module] with $R=B$ and $n=1$, $\mathcal O_X\cong\widetilde B$ as $\mathcal O_X$-modules. By [lem-weil-pbc-pushforward-tilde-spec] applied to $\varphi:A\to B$ and $N=B$, $f_*\mathcal O_X\cong f_*\widetilde B\cong\widetilde{B_A}$, where $B_A$ is $B$ viewed as an $A$-module. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization] with $R=A$, $M=B_A$, the stalk is $(f_*\mathcal O_X)_s\cong(B_A)_{\mathfrak p}$ as an $A_{\mathfrak p}$-module, and $(B_A)_{\mathfrak p}\cong B\otimes_AA_{\mathfrak p}$ (elementary). Finiteness of $B$ over $A$ is not used here or below: the identity holds for every $A$-algebra $B$; the hypothesis is kept for the citer lem-pc-flf-properties.

By the definition of the residue field, $\kappa(s)=A_s/\mathfrak m_sA_s$. Tensoring the quotient presentation with $B$ identifies $B\otimes_A\kappa(s)$ with $(B\otimes_AA_s)\otimes_{A_s}A_s/\mathfrak m_sA_s$, so the stalk tensor in the statement is canonically $B\otimes_A\kappa(s)$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] with $R=A$, $B$ as the first $A$-algebra, and $\kappa(s)$ as the second. It identifies $X\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A\kappa(s))$, and its final clause identifies the global sections of this affine fibre with $B\otimes_A\kappa(s)$. Under these identifications, the canonical map is the identity of this tensor product, hence an isomorphism.
